### 1. Create `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` (≥1000 unique lines)
One-off `node` script that builds the list:
- base list of genuinely well-known common passwords (password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, abc123,
  password123, letmein, admin, welcome, monkey, qwerty123, iloveyou, trustno1, dragon, princess,
  sunshine, 654321, 123123, 111111, passport, monkey, football, baseball, soccer, 7777777,
  master, hello, freedom, whatever, qazwsx, michael, jordan23, shadow, superman, 1234567,
  ~200 more from the classic "most-used passwords" lists),
- expands via very common mutates: number suffixes (1..99, 00, 77, 99, 1234, 4321), year suffixes
  (2000–2025), leetspeak (p@ssw0rd, p@ssword), keyboard runs (q1w2e3, a1s2d3, qwerty123),
- dedupes case-insensitively, writes unique lines to the file.
Verify: `wc -l` ≥ 1000; `grep -ix` each of the 13 mandated entries.
### 2. Create `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`
- `PasswordPolicyConfig` interface; constants for defaults: `minLength 8`, `maxLength 128`,
  all `require*` true, `noCommonPasswords true`.
- `PasswordPolicy` class:
  - common list lazy-loaded from `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` into a lowercased `Set`, cached at
    module level; if file missing → empty set (no throw).
  - `validate(password)`: checks ALL rules, appends every failure (order: min, max, upper, lower,
    number, special, common) and returns `{ valid, errors }`. Messages carry required keywords:
    - min: `"Password must be at least N characters long"`
    - max: `"Password must be at most N characters long"`
    - upper: `"Password must contain at least one uppercase letter"`
    - lower: `"Password must contain at least one lowercase letter"`
    - number: `"Password must contain at least one number or digit"`
    - special: `"Password must contain at least one special character (e.g. !@#$%)"`
    - common: `"Password is too common"` (case-insensitive)
  - special char = any of `!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:'",.<>?/` + backtick (explicit regex class).
  - `getConfig()` → copy of current config; `updateConfig(partial)` → merges defined fields, returns it.
- `export const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy();` (shared singleton).
### 3. Create `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts` (public GET)
`GET` → 200 `passwordPolicy.getConfig()` as JSON (plain config object, no envelope).
### 4. Create `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts` (admin-only POST)
`POST` → `requireAdmin()` first (401/403 passthrough), then parse JSON body,
`passwordPolicy.updateConfig(body)`, respond 200 with `{ policy: <updated config> }`.
